title: Fixed Leading Edge Access Panel Fastener Pattern and Seal Standard

ata.title: Wing Leading Edge — Fixed Leading Edge Structure

abstract: A revised fastener pattern and a bonded seal for the fixed leading edge access panels, ending the elongated holes and water ingress that were forcing panel changes at every heavy check.

sections.reason: Access panels on the fixed leading edge were being changed at a rate of about eleven per aircraft at the twelve-year check, almost all of them for elongated fastener holes at the forward edge. The panels are opened at every slat inspection, which on a high-utilisation aircraft is forty or more times in twelve years, and the anchor nut pattern was never designed for that. Water ingress at the same joint was also producing corrosion on the rib flange underneath at three operators in tropical service.
sections.description: The fastener pitch at the forward edge is reduced from ninety to sixty millimetres and the anchor nuts are replaced by floating items in a bonded strip, so that the load is shared and the panel is no longer located by two fasteners at each corner. The skin panel sub-assembly D5720113135325 is re-drilled to the new pattern and the bracket kit D5720111574269 is added at the two inboard positions where the new pitch needs support. The right-hand doubler OR583107-28 is bonded under the forward edge and the edging grommet EN301916-66 is renewed. A moulded seal replaces the sealant bead at the panel land, which is what stops the water. Microswitch 3VU2 is refitted unchanged. Work is at the left and right wing leading edges in zones 512, 514 and 613. Detail is on drawings D57201139151 and D57201180447.
sections.effects: Mass increase of 5.4 kg per aircraft, symmetric, at a large moment arm but well inside the wing balance tolerance. No electrical effect. Not interchangeable: a post-modification panel will not fit a pre-modification wing and the two must be embodied together side by side. Panel change rate falls to about two per aircraft per heavy check in the trial population. Structure repair content for the panel land changes and the leading edge access task gains a seal condition check.
sections.embodiment_note: Cut into production at MSN S01521. Retrofit is offered at a heavy check only, one hundred and ten manhours per aircraft with both leading edges open, because the wing must be drilled with a jig. Removed panels are scrapped.

type_data.balance_impact: Symmetric; inside the wing balance tolerance
type_data.production_impact: Cut-in at MSN S01521; leading edge drill jig required
